primary.title: Infosys bucks US visa gloom as H-1B approvals soar
primary.description: Infosys recorded more than eightfold increase in approvals for new H-1B employment in the US in fiscal 2026, with the number rising to 2,088 from 257 in the previous financial year, according to federal immigration data cited in a report by The Dallas Express.The Indian IT major was among several employers in Texas that recorded an increase in new H-1B employment approvals during the period. Infosys lists Richardson, Texas, as its petitioner city in the US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) database. However, the records do not establish where all the approved employees will be based.Also Read: IBM gives H-1B, green card holders 3 weeks to relocate from US or leave company; December 31 deadline setThe data also showed an increase in approvals among other private-sector employers. KPMG received 234 approvals for new employment in FY26, compared with 75 in FY25. Texas Instruments saw its approvals rise from 50 to 125, while American Airlines recorded an increase from 60 to 69.The trend was different among some public institutions. UT Southwestern Medical Center recorded 102 approvals for new H-1B employment in FY26, down from 124 in the previous year. Dallas Independent School District also saw its approvals decline from 73 to 39.Also Read: Reality for Indian techies in America: One job, a troublesome H-1B visa, one uncertain futureHowever, the school district's approvals for continuing employment increased to 210 in FY26 from 155 in FY25.Texas plans to ease H-1B hiring curbsThe increase in Infosys' approvals comes as Texas prepares for a possible change in its H-1B visa policy. Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa has said she plans to reverse restrictions introduced by outgoing Governor Greg Abbott on hiring foreign workers through the programme at state agencies and public universities.Abbott issued an executive directive on January 27, 2026, requiring certain state agencies and public universities to obtain written approval from the Texas Workforce Commission (TWC) before filing new H-1B visa petitions.The directive applies to state agencies headed by governor-appointed officials and public institutions of higher education. It was introduced to prioritise qualified Texas residents for state-funded jobs while federal authorities reviewed the H-1B visa programme.The restrictions were scheduled to remain in place until May 31, 2027, unless the TWC granted an exception.In an interview with The Texas Tribune on November 18, Hinojosa said she would rescind the directive after taking office on January 19, 2027. While acknowledging instances of misuse of the H-1B programme, she argued against imposing a blanket restriction.She has not yet outlined what hiring safeguards or reporting requirements could replace Abbott's directive.The proposed reversal could reopen H-1B sponsorship opportunities for foreign professionals, including Indians, seeking jobs with Texas state agencies and public universities.However, the proposed policy change does not directly affect private-sector employers such as Infosys, which are outside the scope of Abbott's restrictions. It also does not change federal H-1B eligibility or approval requirements.
